benchmark_cost.definition: per benchmark, mean over models with an observed cell of the per-(model, benchmark) value; cost_tokens = sum over sub-runs (leaf tables) of '# eval' x ('# prompt tokens' + '# output tokens'), one pass (one in-context-example trial), model-specific tokenizers
benchmark_cost.requests_per_instance_note: median over models of num_requests / (instances x trials summed over all splits and perturbed copies), from runs.json; 1 where every run uses generation or multiple_choice_joint and runs.json reports no num_requests

GSM8K.group_description: The grade school math word problems dataset (GSM8K) for testing mathematical reasoning on grade-school math problems [(Cobbe et al., 2021)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2110.14168.pdf).
GSM8K.metric_description: Fraction of instances that the predicted output matches a correct reference exactly, ignoring text preceding the specified indicator.

LegalBench.group_description: LegalBench is a large collaboratively constructed benchmark of legal reasoning tasks [(Guha et al, 2023)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2308.11462.pdf).
LegalBench.metric_description: Fraction of instances that the predicted output matches a correct reference up to light processing.

MATH.group_description: The MATH benchmark for measuring mathematical problem solving on competition math problems with chain-of-thought style reasoning [(Hendrycks et al., 2021)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2103.03874.pdf).
MATH.metric_description: Fraction of model outputs that are mathematically equivalent to the correct reference when using chain-of-thought prompting.

MMLU.group_description: The Massive Multitask Language Understanding (MMLU) benchmark for knowledge-intensive question answering across 57 domains [(Hendrycks et al., 2021)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2009.03300.pdf).
MMLU.metric_description: Fraction of instances that the predicted output matches a correct reference exactly.

MedQA.group_description: MedQA is an open domain question answering dataset composed of questions from professional medical board exams ([Jin et al. 2020](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2009.13081.pdf)).
MedQA.metric_description: Fraction of instances that the predicted output matches a correct reference up to light processing.

NarrativeQA.group_description: The NarrativeQA benchmark for reading comprehension over narratives [(Kočiský et al., 2017)](https://aclanthology.org/Q18-1023/).
NarrativeQA.metric_description: Average F1 score in terms of word overlap between the model output and correct reference.

NaturalQuestions (closed-book).group_description: The NaturalQuestions [(Kwiatkowski et al., 2019)](https://aclanthology.org/Q19-1026/) benchmark for question answering based on naturally-occurring queries through Google Search. The input does not include the Wikipedia page with the answer.
NaturalQuestions (closed-book).metric_description: Average F1 score in terms of word overlap between the model output and correct reference.

NaturalQuestions (open-book).group_description: The NaturalQuestions [(Kwiatkowski et al., 2019)](https://aclanthology.org/Q19-1026/) benchmark for question answering based on naturally-occurring queries through Google Search. The input includes the Wikipedia page with the answer.
NaturalQuestions (open-book).metric_description: Average F1 score in terms of word overlap between the model output and correct reference.

OpenbookQA.group_description: The OpenbookQA benchmark for commonsense-intensive open book question answering [(Mihaylov et al., 2018)](https://aclanthology.org/D18-1260/).
OpenbookQA.metric_description: Fraction of instances that the predicted output matches a correct reference exactly.

WMT 2014.group_description: WMT 2014 is a collection of machine translation datasets [(website)](https://www.statmt.org/wmt14/index.html).
WMT 2014.metric_description: Average BLEU score [(Papineni et al., 2002)](https://aclanthology.org/P02-1040/) based on 4-gram overlap.

caveats: 'Mean win rate' (column 11 of data/helm.csv) is not a benchmark and depends on the model set, so it is not a column here; it is kept as models[*].mean_win_rate.

Release dates of Mistral Large/Small 2402, Mistral Large 2407 and GPT-4o (2024-05-13) are corrected from upstream typos (2023-02-26, 2023-07-24, 2024-04-09) to the date in the model id (RELEASE_DATE_OVERRIDES; models[*].release_date_upstream).

HELM renamed 6 of the 30 snapshot models (e.g. 'Anthropic Claude 2.0' -> 'Claude 2.0', 'Cohere Command' -> 'Command'); models[*].snapshot_display_name gives the name used in data/helm.csv and data/canonical_mapping.json.
One missing cell: Phi-3 (7B) has no GSM8K run.
Instances differ by model for LegalBench (1562 instead of 2047 for Mistral Large/Small 2402) and WMT 2014 (Jamba Instruct lacks fr-en: 2341 instead of 2844).
Token counts use each model's own tokenizer; the per-benchmark cost vector averages over models.
Data license unresolved: HELM's code is Apache-2.0, but the benchmark_output JSON states no terms for redistributing the score tables; check before the data release.

Raw inputs are pinned by GCS object generation, but the bucket keeps only the current generation (HELM rewrote all release files in 2026). After HELM's next rewrite '--fetch --pin-manifest' will fail; the sha256 values (source.raw_inputs, raw_manifests/<name>.json) then only verify archived copies, so the raw directory (~92 MB for the three HELM matrices) should be archived with the data release.

cell_costs.layout: lists [model][benchmark] aligned with model_names x benchmark_names; null where unobserved (leaderboard_value: HELM's displayed score, only where it differs from B)

release_date_vs_model_id.rule: a release date conflicts with the date in the model id if it is more than 7 days earlier or more than 60 days later (YYMM ids: than the month), or, for OpenAI MMDD ids, has another month-day

runs_json_cross_check.note: runs.json value of each observed cell (the cell's runs; see score_definition) vs the leaderboard value, and runs.json costs vs leaf-table costs; cost differences are expected only in leaderboard_differences cells and in cells with sub_splits (CivilComments)

snapshot.conclusion: identical: every snapshot model keeps its v1.0.0 runs and scores
